title: Explainable AI
overview: Learn why model decisions need explanation and survey methods for interpreting predictions.
objectives: Distinguish interpretable models from post-hoc explanations
Describe feature importance and local explanations

method.title: Why explain
method.body: Explanations support debugging, trust, regulatory compliance, and detecting spurious correlations.

method.title: Interpretable models
method.body: Linear models and small trees can be read directly, often at some cost in predictive power.

method.title: Post-hoc methods
method.body: Permutation importance, partial dependence, and local surrogate methods estimate how inputs affect outputs.

method.title: Caveats
method.body: Explanations can be unstable or misleading and should be validated, not treated as ground truth.

pseudocode:
base = score(model, X, y)
for feature in features:
    Xp = shuffle_column(X, feature)
    importance[feature] = base - score(model, Xp, y)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
X = rng.normal(size=(200, 2))
y = (X[:,0] > 0).astype(int)
pred = lambda M: (M[:,0] > 0).astype(int)
base = (pred(X) == y).mean()
for j in range(2):
    Xp = X.copy(); rng.shuffle(Xp[:,j])
    print('feature', j, 'accuracy drop:', round(base - (pred(Xp)==y).mean(), 2))
